title: Profiling Snapshot Orchestrator and Export Harness
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a lightweight orchestration layer (profiling-snapshot-orchestrator) and an export harness designed to collect short-duration profiling snapshots across a distributed serving cluster. The goal is to capture representative traces and flamegraphs with minimal interference to latency SLOs, automatically aggregate artifacts, and push them to our perf CI bucket for postmortem and regression detection runs.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Existing profilers produce large, long-running captures that perturb production latency or require manual coordination.
- We need frequent, short, synchronized snapshots (2–8s) across a set of replicas to observe KV cache behavior, batching hotspots, and cross-node tail latency correlations.
- Snapshot data should be exported in a standardized artifact format (collapsed flame, pprof, otlp-export) and ingested by the CI/analysis pipelines.

High-level design:
- Orchestrator (go binary + small python CLI): schedules snapshot windows across a target set of nodes, coordinates tracer start/stop, and attaches metadata (route, model, seq_len_dist, commit).
- Collector agent (lightweight daemon on each host): interfaces with ptrace/perf, eBPF sampler, or runtime instrument hooks and writes local snapshot bundles to /tmp/prof-snapshots/<run-id>/.
- Aggregator + exporter: pulls node bundles, normalizes timestamps, deduplicates stack frames, generates collapsed flame files, and uploads to perf-ci S3 prefix: s3://redwood-perf-ci/snapshots/<commit>/<run-id>/
- CI integration: perf CI job downloads latest snapshot artifacts, runs artifact diffs against baseline, and kicks off alerting if regressions found.

Key properties and constraints:
- Snapshot duration: default 5s (configurable per job).
- Low overhead target: <1% p99 latency increase when snapshotting (empirically measured on xavier-32).
- Rate limiting: orchestrator ensures only a limited fraction of machines snap at once to avoid cluster-wide noise.
- Security: all agents run under redwood-agent user; exports must be signed.

Components and files (implementation notes):
- cmd/ps-orch/main.go: lightweight HTTP API (start, stop, status, list-runs) and scheduler.
- agent/collector.py: small Python helper to invoke perf/eBPF probes and collect /proc, env, runtime stats.
- tools/aggregator/bin/aggregate_snapshots: normalizes bundles and emits collapsed-flame.txt + pprof.pb.
- ci/jobs/perf-snapshots.yml: CI job that downloads latest snapshots and runs compare-snapshots.py.

Example workflow (manual run):
1) Select target set via tag or service name: 
   ./ps-orch start --service=serving-runtime --tag=canary --duration=5s --sample-rate=10
2) Orchestrator returns run-id (e.g., run-20241102-04f2).
3) Agent on each selected host writes to /tmp/prof-snapshots/run-20241102-04f2/*.tar.gz with files: collapsed-flame.txt, pprof.pb, host-meta.json, runtime-metrics.json.
4) Aggregator: aggregate_snapshots --input-dir /tmp/prof-snapshots/run-20241102-04f2 --out s3://redwood-perf-ci/snapshots/20241102/04f2/ --normalize-stacks
5) CI: perf-snapshots.yml pulls artifacts and runs compare-snapshots.py --baseline s3://redwood-perf-ci/baselines/serving-runtime/20241020 --alert-on-regression 10

Collector hints and safe defaults:
- Use perf record -F 99 -g -- sleep <duration> for native stacks when kernel symbols available. Fall back to eBPF stack sampling when perf cannot attach.
- For runtime stacks (Go/C++), use runtime/pprof endpoints where available (pprof.GetProfile) or call into our runtime trace hook.
- Capture a tiny /proc snapshot (cpuinfo, meminfo), the process open file descriptors count, and the current KV cache stats (kvcache.hot_entries, misses_last_60s).
- Write host-meta.json with keys: hostname, instance_type, machine_id, git_commit, docker_image, route_hash, seq_len_p50,p95. These are necessary for later correlation.

Aggregator behavior (important):
- Normalize symbol names by stripping sandboxes and dynamic loader prefixes.
- Merge stacks with identical traces across hosts to build a cluster-level flame. Keep per-host flames as well.
- Compute a simple attribution breakdown: tokenize by module (runtime, dispatcher, kvcache, gpu-kernel, syscalls) and show percent CPU.
- Emit both collapsed-flame (for speedscope/FlameGraph.pl) and pprof proto for deeper analysis.

CI job example (ci/jobs/perf-snapshots.yml) excerpt:
# Note: simplified pseudo-yaml for clarity
# job: compare recent snapshots vs baseline
steps:
  - checkout
  - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-perf-ci/snapshots/${COMMIT}/${RUN_ID}/ /tmp/snapshots/ --recursive
  - python tools/compare-snapshots.py --new /tmp/snapshots --baseline s3://redwood-perf-ci/baselines/${SERVICE}/${BASELINE_ID} --threshold 8 --output /tmp/report.json
  - if report indicates regression: notify #perf-alerts and open JIRA PERF-<auto>

Practical tips for low-noise captures:
- Stagger sampling start times by 50–300ms across replicas to avoid synchronized GC spikes. Orchestrator can provide jitter seeds.
- When profiling GPU paths, prefer NVTX ranges emitted by runtime to localize kernel launches; eBPF stacktrace for userland may miss device-side time.
- Keep snapshot windows short and repeat more frequently instead of long captures; this reduces perturbation while increasing representativeness.

Ad-hoc debugging mode (developer flow):
- Start orchestrator against a single node: ./ps-orch start --hosts host-123 --duration=8s --sample-rate=1 --debug- Download artifacts and use: 
    flamegraph.pl collapsed-flame.txt > host-123-flame.svg
    pprof -http=:8081 pprof.pb
- Use the provided parse_kvcache.py to overlay kvcache hit/miss timelines on the flamegraph HTML output.

Common failure modes and triage checklist:
- No artifact produced on host  : check collector.log for permission errors or perf attach failures; ensure redwood-agent user in perf_event group.
- Empty flame (only syscalls): missing symbols; run symbolizer container or mount /usr/lib/debug.
- Large bundle size (>50MB): agent fell back to trace-buffer dump; reduce pprof frequency or compress with zstd.
- CI compare job failing with parse errors: check host-meta.json schema changes (seq_len fields recent rename).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical baseline cadence for snapshots (weekly vs per-merge).
- Add automatic correlation with infra metrics (netpackets, disk-io) in aggregator.
- Should we add a continuous low-rate sampling mode that writes to a ring buffer (for longer-term trend detection)?
- Formalize alert thresholds per route/model rather than global threshold.

Notes-to-self / quick commands:
- Trigger quick smoke across canary pool: ./ps-orch start --service=serving-runtime --tag=canary --duration=3s --parallelism=0.25
- Re-run aggregator locally: tools/aggregate_snapshots --input-dir /tmp/prof-snapshots/run-id --out /tmp/out --normalize-stacks
- Example S3 layout: s3://redwood-perf-ci/snapshots/<commit>/<run-id>/{hostA,hostB}/collapsed-flame.txt

References and related docs:
- RFC-724 distributed-profiling-snapshots (design rationale)
- github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-profiling (collector code + test harness)
- Confluence: /display/PERF/Profiling+Tooling+Index

End of doc.
